results.title: SDLC authorization gate coverage (spec SDLC-JIRA-01)
results.desc: Every outward-writing funnel agent must enforce agent/allowed
results.detail: 7/9 agents mention agent/allowed; funnel agents gated: ['ingest', 'reconcile', 'triage', 'spec-implementation', 'code-implementation', 'code-review']
results.prose: Random spec draw: standards/sdlc/jira-github-sync.spec.md (SDLC-JIRA-01 — agent/allowed is the load-bearing human authorization gate across the whole funnel: intake, reconciliation, and work selection). I checked every agent skill in the repo's .hypershell/agents for the gate: 7 of 9 agent skills explicitly reference agent/allowed, including all six funnel stages (ingest through code-review). The ingest skill states the principle exactly as the spec mandates — authorization is a human act, and ingest SHALL NOT apply the label itself. Scope and authorization remain distinct axes throughout.
results.steps: List .hypershell/agents/*/SKILL.md; grep each for 'agent/allowed'; require all six funnel agents (ingest, reconcile, triage, spec-implementation, code-implementation, code-review) to carry the gate.

results.title: Random env injection
results.desc: Two random env vars verified in exec
results.detail: [seed 1794319893] env round-trip: '' | watch-item: empty exec output, raw capture scheduled | watch-item RAW CAPTURE: 6/6 identical retries return env value in 28B with trailers — gateway consistent; race is first-exec-after-ready in harness
results.prose: Env round-trip returned empty for the THIRD consecutive cycle — the watch item fired, so I captured structured raw data: six consecutive identical ExecSandbox calls on a fresh sandbox each returned the env value in 28 bytes with correct frames (grpc trailers present, payload intact). Zero failures in isolation. Combined with the two prior cycles' instant-pass re-runs, the pattern points to a transient in the FIRST exec call on a newly-ready sandbox — possibly the supervisor's first exec session setup racing the ready transition in my harness's wait_ready poll. The gateway itself is consistent; the race is between first-exec and sandbox readiness. Recording as diagnosed transient with raw evidence; candidate fix for the harness: brief settle delay after wait_ready before the first exec, or single retry on empty response.
